title: Kahana vs Podia: The Cohort Needs a Shelf

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Used by creators to sell digital products, courses, memberships, and communities.
Pricing (2026): Mover ≈USD 42/mo annual (USD 49 monthly); Shaker ≈USD 84/mo annual (USD 99 monthly); Earthquaker ≈USD 150/mo annual (USD 179 monthly).

strengths.title: All-in-one for small creators
strengths.detail: No-code site + courses + coaching + webinars + memberships + community + email, a solid starter stack for solo creators.

strengths.title: Simple, transparent product structure
strengths.detail: Easy to create courses, digital products, and community spaces without complex setup.

strengths.title: Built-in email marketing
strengths.detail: Broadcasts and campaigns included; free up to a certain subscriber count.

strengths.title: Flexible pricing tiers
strengths.detail: Plans with varying transaction fees so creators can match expected sales volume.

weaknesses.title: Pricing and fee complexity
weaknesses.detail: Subscription costs plus transaction fees require careful cost modeling.

weaknesses.title: Feature depth vs higher-end platforms
weaknesses.detail: Community and course tooling can be less sophisticated than Kajabi, Thinkific, or Skool for some use cases.

weaknesses.title: Free plan removed
weaknesses.detail: No free plan as of late 2024, higher barrier to entry than before.

weaknesses.title: Limited design flexibility
weaknesses.detail: Simpler templates; less custom branding than dedicated site builders.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Podia is course hosting, drip, enrollment, and lesson checkout. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Podia is a simple all-in-one platform to build a no-code website, create and sell online courses, and host a free or paid community.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Podia side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Podia you can use Courses, Memberships, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with Podia

You can use both. Podia keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on Podia for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. Podia stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
